Operating Characteristics of the Comb-BOIN12 Design

Source: R/sim_comb_boin12.R
sim_comb_boin12.Rd

Simulate trials of the Comb-BOIN12 design of Lu et al. (2025) for two drugs given together with comb_boin12_simulate, select the optimal biological dose combination (OBDC) of every trial with comb_boin12_select_obd, and summarize the selection percentages and the numbers of patients, DLTs and responses at every combination.

Usage

sim_comb_boin12(
  target,
  target_resp,
  p_true,
  p_resp,
  n_cohort,
  cohort_size,
  n_trials = 10000,
  start_dose = c(1, 1),
  n_earlystop = NULL,
  n_earlystop_rule = c("with_stay", "simple"),
  p_saf = NULL,
  p_tox = NULL,
  cutoff_eli = 0.95,
  cutoff_eli_resp = 0.9,
  extrasafe = FALSE,
  offset = 0.05,
  psi00 = 40,
  psi11 = 60,
  benchmark_weight = 0.5,
  utility_prior = c(1, 1),
  n_star = 6,
  tie_break = c("higher", "random"),
  no_candidate = c("nearest", "stop"),
  resp_cor = 0,
  resp_cor_type = c("copula", "binary"),
  est_method = c("logistic", "observed"),
  obd_bound = c("rectangle", "contour"),
  dose_a = NULL,
  dose_b = NULL,
  logistic_scale = c(2.5, 2.5),
  n_draws = 4000,
  keep_trials = FALSE,
  verbose = FALSE,
  seed = 123
)

Arguments

target

Numeric scalar. Highest acceptable DLT probability, phi_T. It is the target of the BOIN boundaries lambda_e and lambda_d, of the admissibility of a combination and of the MTD combination that bounds the OBD combination.

target_resp

Numeric scalar. Lowest acceptable response probability, phi_E, as in sim_boin12.

p_true

Numeric matrix. True DLT probability of every combination, with one row per level of drug A and one column per level of drug B.

p_resp

Numeric matrix of the same size. True response probability of every combination.

n_cohort

Integer scalar. Number of cohorts in a trial.

cohort_size

Integer scalar or vector. Number of patients per cohort. A scalar is used for every cohort; a shorter vector is padded with its last element.

n_trials

Integer scalar. Number of trials to simulate. Defaults to 10000.

start_dose

Integer vector of length 2. Levels of drug A and drug B of the first cohort. Defaults to c(1, 1).

n_earlystop

Integer scalar or NULL. Number of patients at the current combination that ends the trial when the next cohort would stay there (see n_earlystop_rule). Defaults to NULL, which runs every trial to the maximum sample size, as in Lu et al. (2025).

n_earlystop_rule

Character scalar. "with_stay" (the default) ends the trial at n_earlystop only when the next cohort would stay at the current combination; "simple" ends it in any case.

p_saf, p_tox

Numeric scalars or NULL. Highest DLT probability deemed subtherapeutic and lowest deemed overly toxic, which give the BOIN boundaries. Default to 0.6 * target and 1.4 * target.

cutoff_eli

Numeric scalar. A combination is inadmissible, together with every combination with at least the same levels of both drugs, when the posterior probability that its DLT rate exceeds target is at least this cutoff. Defaults to 0.95.

cutoff_eli_resp

Numeric scalar. A combination is inadmissible when the posterior probability that its response rate is below target_resp is at least this cutoff. Defaults to 0.90.

extrasafe

Logical scalar. Apply the cutoff cutoff_eli - offset to the lowest combination, as Lu et al. (2025) do with 0.85. Defaults to FALSE.

offset

Numeric scalar. Amount by which cutoff_eli is lowered at the lowest combination when extrasafe is TRUE. Defaults to 0.05, as in sim_comb_boin; Lu et al. (2025) use 0.10.

psi00, psi11

Numeric scalars from 0 to 100. Utility of a patient without DLT and without response, and with both, as in sim_boin12. Default to 40 and 60. The utility pE - wT * pT of Lu et al. (2025) is psi00 = 100 * wT / (1 + wT) and psi11 = 100 / (1 + wT); their wT = 0.11 is psi00 = 9.90991 and psi11 = 90.09009.

benchmark_weight

Numeric scalar above 0 and at most 1. Weight of the lowest acceptable utility in the utility benchmark, as in sim_boin12; it is the weight w_u of Lu et al. (2025), who use 0.6. Defaults to 0.5.

utility_prior

Numeric vector of two positive numbers. Beta prior of the utility of a combination divided by 100. Defaults to c(1, 1).

n_star

Integer scalar. With at least this many patients at the current combination and a DLT rate between lambda_e and lambda_d, the next combination is chosen from the current one and the two below it. Defaults to 6.

tie_break

Character scalar. Choice among the combinations of equal desirability: "higher" (the default) keeps those with the highest sum of the two levels and draws one of them at random when several remain; "random" draws one of all the tied combinations. See Details.

no_candidate

Character scalar. What happens when none of the combinations allowed for the next cohort is admissible: "nearest" (the default) goes to the admissible combination nearest to the current one; "stop" ends the trial without an OBD combination. See Details.

resp_cor

Numeric scalar between -1 and 1. Correlation between the DLT and the response of a patient, see resp_cor_type. Defaults to 0.

resp_cor_type

Character scalar. "copula" (the default) or "binary", as in sim_boin12.

est_method

Character scalar. Estimate of the response probability: "logistic" (the default) the posterior mean under the logistic model of Lu et al. (2025), see Details; "observed" the observed response rate.

obd_bound

Character scalar. Combinations from which the OBDC is chosen: "rectangle" (the default) those with both levels at most those of the MTDC, as Lu et al. (2025) write; "contour" those, in every column (level of drug B), at most the combination of that column whose isotonic DLT rate is closest to target, the rule that reproduces the results published by Lu et al. (2025). See Details.

dose_a, dose_b

Numeric vectors or NULL. Dose values of the levels of drug A and of drug B in the logistic model. Default to NULL, the level numbers. Each is standardized to mean 0 and standard deviation 0.5.

logistic_scale

Numeric vector of two positive numbers. Scales of the Cauchy priors of the intercept and of the other coefficients of the logistic model. Defaults to c(2.5, 2.5), as in Lu et al. (2025).

n_draws

Integer scalar. Number of points of the importance sampling of the logistic model. Defaults to 4000.

keep_trials

Logical scalar. Keep the simulated trials (trials) and the selected combinations (obd) in the result. Defaults to FALSE.

verbose

Logical scalar. Print progress messages. Defaults to FALSE.

seed

Integer scalar or NULL. Random seed. The state of the calling session is restored on exit. Defaults to 123.

Value

An object of class comb_boin12_oc, which is a list with components

design

"Comb-BOIN12".

target, target_resp, p_true, p_resp

The limits and the true probabilities.

n_rows, n_cols, n_trials

Numbers of levels of drug A and drug B, and of trials.

lambda_e, lambda_d, u_benchmark

The BOIN boundaries and the utility benchmark (scale 0 to 100).

sel_percent

Matrix of the percentage of trials selecting each combination as the OBDC.

percent_no_obd, percent_early_stop

Percentages of trials selecting no OBDC and stopped early.

n_pts_dose, n_tox_dose, n_resp_dose

Matrices of the average numbers of patients, DLTs and responses at each combination.

total_n_pts, total_n_tox, total_n_resp

Their totals.

true_obd

Two-column matrix of the true OBDCs: the combinations with the highest true utility among those with a DLT probability at most target.

pct_true_obd_selected, pct_patients_true_obd

Percentage of trials selecting a true OBDC and percentage of the patients treated there.

overdose

List with the cutoff (target), the combinations above it, and the percentages of trials selecting one of them (pct_selected) and of patients treated there (pct_patients).

stop_reason_percent

Percentage of trials by stopping reason.

est_method, obd_bound, settings, call

The settings used.

trials, obd

With keep_trials = TRUE, the comb_boin12_trials object and a two-column matrix of the selected combinations.

Details

The percentages of patients are those of the average numbers of patients. Lu et al. (2025) report the average over trials of the number of patients as a percentage of the maximum sample size; with keep_trials = TRUE it can be computed from trials, as in inst/reproduce/reproduce_Lu2025.R.

With the logistic estimate, each trial takes a few milliseconds to select; est_method = "observed" is much faster.

References

Lu, M., Zhang, J., Yuan, Y. and Lin, R. (2025). Comb-BOIN12: A utility-based Bayesian optimal interval design for dose optimization in cancer drug-combination trials. Statistics in Biopharmaceutical Research, 17(2), 266-276. doi:10.1080/19466315.2024.2370403

See also

sim_comb_boin12_multi, comb_boin12_simulate, comb_boin12_select_obd, print.comb_boin12_oc

Examples

# Scenario 16 of Lu et al. (2025), with their design settings
p_true <- matrix(c(0.05, 0.10, 0.15, 0.15, 0.20, 0.45), nrow = 2)
p_resp <- matrix(c(0.10, 0.20, 0.30, 0.40, 0.50, 0.60), nrow = 2)
oc <- sim_comb_boin12(
  target = 0.33, target_resp = 0.2, p_true = p_true, p_resp = p_resp,
  n_cohort = 14, cohort_size = 3, n_trials = 200,
  psi00 = 100 * 0.11 / 1.11, psi11 = 100 / 1.11, benchmark_weight = 0.6,
  extrasafe = TRUE, offset = 0.10, dose_a = c(100, 200),
  dose_b = c(50, 100, 200), seed = 123
)
oc
